item.title: Guilty plea on federal charges in deadly Boulder firebomb attack
item.description: The man who already pleaded guilty to more than 100 state criminal charges, including first-degree murder, for an attack on the Pearl Street Mall in June 2025, appeared in federal court on Thursday where he changed his plea to guilty on a dozen charges.

item.title: Live Updates: Trump campaigns in South Carolina and more
item.description: More than 42 million Americans had voted early as of Thursday afternoon, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.

item.title: 9 major companies ordered to share how they use personal data to set prices or pay workers
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission has ordered nine major companies to turn over detailed information that will determine whether they are using users' personal data to charge them more or pay their employees less. MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more details.

item.title: Patrick Stewart, best known for "Star Trek" and "X-Men," dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart starred on stage and screen across his decadeslong acting career. He died at his home on Wednesday.

item.title: Walking through Patrick Stewart's career, from celebrated thespian to "Star Trek" icon
item.description: Sir Patrick Stewart, the iconic actor, royal knight and thespian, who spent more time on stage than he did on screens, has died at 86. Wall Street Journal reporter Chris Kornelis joins "The Daily Report" to discuss his career.

item.title: Details on Flávio Bolsonaro's escape from Brazil
item.description: CBS News' Lilia Luciano has the details on how Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, managed to flee the country for Florida, despite being asked to turn over his passports to Brazilian authorities.

item.title: Is it legal to recruit a candidate with the same name as one's opponent?
item.description: Alaska's governor ordered a new investigation into the alleged plot to siphon votes away from Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, as the Justice Department issued new subpoenas in the case. CBS News legal analyst Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Trump cancels Iowa rally, will hold telerallies instead
item.description: President Trump canceled his rally in Iowa, opting for a telerally instead. He also spoke at a rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina, on Thursday afternoon, where he campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Darline Graham. CBS News' Fin Gómez reports and Nicholas Reynolds, a politics editor for The Post and Courier, has more on South Carolina's Senate race.

item.title: Millions of French press coffee makers recalled due to burn risk
item.description: Product safety regulators said the glass carafes can unexpectedly break if they are damaged or cracked, leading to burn injuries.

item.title: 2 choppers involved in midair collision near Oregon airport, officials say
item.description: Two helicopters collided in midair on Thursday afternoon in a community near Portland, Oregon.

item.title: Linda Mason, CBS News veteran and trailblazing journalist, dies at age 84
item.description: After starting as a radio desk assistant in 1966, Linda Mason went on to become the first female producer of the "CBS Evening News" and held several other high-profile positions at CBS News.

item.title: You are cordially invited to crash a wedding: site helps fill empty seats at ceremonies
item.description: A new service connects people who love love with soon-to-be married couples who have open seats. Not a Wedding Crasher lists dozens of ceremonies all over the country. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Linda Mason, trailblazer for female journalists, dies at 84
item.description: Journalist Linda Mason has died at 84. She was a pioneer behind the scenes over a nearly 50-year career, including on the "CBS Evening News" with Walter Cronkite.

item.title: Social media stunt backfires as public sides with hardworking father instead
item.description: Teens with cameras played a cruel prank on a father stocking shelves at a Michigan grocery store. But the dad told them off in a video that's inspired a huge response from fed-up people everywhere. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: DOJ issues new subpoenas in Alaska Senate probe
item.description: The Justice Department has begun issuing a new wave of subpoenas stemming from an ongoing criminal investigation into Alaska's U.S. Senate race, multiple sources confirmed to CBS News.

item.title: Latest on manhunt for escaped Tennessee convicted murderer
item.description: Nearly four days after Jacob Morley's brazen escape from prison in Tennessee, the convicted murderer was still on the loose Thursday. Ian Lee reports on the latest details in the search.

item.title: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner over alleged leaks
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a Pentagon official told CBS News.

item.title: Hegseth fires another top military general as critics raise alarm
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's aggressive and, what critics call, dangerous overhaul of the U.S. military continued this week. Top military strategist Lt. General Brett Sylvia was abruptly fired, accused of leaking classified information to the media. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: 8-year-old girl chokes to death at Texas school
item.description: An 8-year-old girl choked on lunch in her Texas elementary school cafeteria and died in April. Jason Allen reports on the newly-released footage.

item.title: Trump campaigns in South Carolina as Senate race is surprisingly close
item.description: The critical Senate race in South Carolina is closer than expected, and President Trump stopped there with six days to go until the midterms. Weijia Jiang has more.

item.title: Details on the controversy upending Alaska's key Senate race
item.description: The Justice Department has issued subpoenas into allegations that people associated with the Alaska Senate campaign of Democrat Mary Peltola launched an effort to confuse Republican voters by recruiting a spoiler candidate who shared the Republican incumbent's name. Jonah Kaplan reports from Petersburg, Alaska.

item.title: In tight Kansas Senate race, struggling farmers are split
item.description: Rising fertilizer and fuel costs, drought and low crop prices have pushed Kansas farms to the edge — scrambling farmers' loyalties in the Senate race between GOP Sen. Roger Marshall and Democrat Adam Hamilton.

item.title: Looking back at Patrick Stewart's legendary career
item.description: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known as Captain Picard in "Star Trek" and Professor X in the "X-Men" movies, has died at 86. A spokesperson said he died in Los Angeles after a battle with Alzheimer's disease and dementia. Vladimir Duthiers looks back at his life and legacy.

item.title: Google parent company's stock falls nearly 13% in worst day since company went public
item.description: Alphabet, Google's parent company, lost 13% of its stock value in one day amid AI-related investor concerns. CBS News contributor Javier David has more.

item.title: WNBA criticized after WNBA Finals game scheduled during lunchtime: "They dropped the ball"
item.description: The Atlanta Dream won Game 6 of the WNBA Finals in front of a sold-out crowd Thursday, but they played the game at lunchtime in Atlanta. Mark Strassmann reports on the scheduling controversy.

item.title: What early voting numbers tell us about the midterms as campaigns make final push
item.description: CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto, and the head of data science at VoteHub, Zachary Donnini, break down early voting numbers with just days to go before the midterms.

item.title: California officials face grand jury subpoenas as DOJ expands voting probe
item.description: The Justice Department has issued grand jury subpoenas to California officials, escalating a dispute over allegations by the federal government that the state may have as many as 20,000 non-citizens registered to vote.

item.title: Midterm elections put Social Security funding gaps on the ballot
item.description: With Social Security's main trust fund on course to be depleted in 2032, Congress will face mounting pressure to find remedies and avert benefit cuts.

item.title: Midterm races in Alaska, South Carolina heat up as Trump steps in
item.description: Alaska is investigating Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign over a candidate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent. Meanwhile, President Trump is campaigning for Darline Graham in South Carolina. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe and Weijia Jiang have more.

item.title: 10/29: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Alaska Senate race under investigation amid Dan Sullivan controversy; Trump's Iran war drives up airfares as midterms approach.
